title: 2007 Fiesta Bowl: How Boise State Beat OU 43-42 in Overtime
question: What happened in the 2007 Fiesta Bowl between Oklahoma and Boise State?
answer: Unbeaten Boise State beat Oklahoma 43-42 in overtime on January 1, 2007, tying the game with a hook-and-lateral in the final seconds and winning on a Statue of Liberty two-point conversion.
summary: Boise State beat Oklahoma 43-42 in OT at the Jan. 1, 2007 Fiesta Bowl using a hook-and-lateral, a halfback pass and the Statue of Liberty play to finish.
body: Sooner fans would rather not relive it, but the 2007 Fiesta Bowl is one of the most replayed games in college football. Big 12 champion Oklahoma, ranked seventh and favored by more than a touchdown, faced ninth-ranked, unbeaten WAC champion Boise State in Glendale, Arizona.

Boise State built an 18-point lead, but Oklahoma rallied to tie the game at 28 in the final minutes. Then cornerback Marcus Walker intercepted Jared Zabransky and returned it for a touchdown, giving OU a 35-28 lead with 1:02 left. Boise State faced fourth-and-18 near midfield with seconds remaining and called a hook-and-lateral: Zabransky hit Drisan James, who flipped the ball to Jerard Rabb for the tying touchdown.

Adrian Peterson opened overtime with a 25-yard touchdown run, his final college score, for a 42-35 lead. Boise State answered on fourth down when receiver Vinny Perretta threw a touchdown pass to Derek Schouman, and coach Chris Petersen chose to go for the win. On the two-point try, Zabransky faked a pass and handed the ball behind his back to Ian Johnson, who scored on the Statue of Liberty play.
Boise State finished 13-0, while Oklahoma ended 11-3. ESPN later recalled one more twist: right after the game, Johnson proposed to his girlfriend, a Boise State cheerleader.
